title: mattpocock/skills: engineering skills from one working .agents folder
friendlyTitle: mattpocock/skills: ready-made instructions for a coding agent
summary: Matt Pocock's skills repository gained 882 stars on GitHub Trending on 1 November, and has about 308,200 in total. It is the skill set from his own .agents directory, under MIT. The engineering skills include a pull-request shape and a wizard for steps only a person can do, such as creating credentials. The productivity skills include grilling a plan until the open branches are resolved, and compacting a session into a handoff another agent can continue.
friendlySummary: Matt Pocock's skills repository gained 882 stars on GitHub Trending on 1 November, and has about 308,200 in total. It is the instruction set from his own agent folder, under the MIT license. The coding skills include how to write a pull request and a guided script for steps only a person can do, such as creating passwords for a service. The work skills include questioning a plan until the open choices are settled, and writing a handoff so another agent can continue.
whyItMatters: Install the set into the agent you already use, rather than copying one skill into a prompt. Claude Code, Codex, and Copilot can install from the repository's marketplace. Gemini and the skills.sh route are updated by hand. The skills tell the agent how to write a pull request or interview you about a design. They do not review the code for you, and they do not replace a test.
